formulas.name: Monte Carlo likelihood approximation (Geyer and Thompson 1992)
formulas.where: The log-likelihood ratio relative to \(\eta\) is estimated from simulated statistics; the approximation maximized in each round replaces the intractable normalizing constant. formulas.name: Metropolis-Hastings toggle step (Hastings 1970; Snijders 2002)
formulas.where: \(y'\) is \(y\) with one dyad toggled and \(q\) is the proposal distribution of the dyad to toggle; the proposal rule changes the chain but not its stationary distribution \(\Pr_\theta\). formulas.name: Simulated mean statistics

formulas.name: Description length (Peixoto 2017; degree correction after Karrer and Newman 2011)
formulas.latex: \Sigma(A,b)=-\ln P(A\mid e,b)-\ln P(e)-\ln P(b)\quad\bigl[-\ln P(k\mid e,b)\ \text{added, with }P(A\mid k,e,b),\ \text{for the degree-corrected model}\bigr]
formulas.where: The negative log of the joint probability of the network, the block edge counts, the partition and (degree-corrected) the degrees, with the microcanonical Bayesian priors of the paper; it is in nats. The components are reported separately: adjacency, partition, edges, degrees. The closed forms of the components are in the paper and are not transcribed here.

formulas.name: Fit as minimization
formulas.where: The partition (and its number of blocks) with the shortest description length. The exact minimizer is found only by exhaustive search on tiny graphs; heuristics return a local minimum.

variants.sbm_fit: Blocks, their number and the description length of the best partition found over several restarts.

notation.meaning: \(x\) with the tie variable \((i,j)\) toggled; \(x^{(ii)}=x\) means no change
rate of change opportunities of actor \(i\)

formulas.name: Stochastic actor-oriented model (Snijders 2001; Snijders 1996)
formulas.latex: \Pr(i\text{ toggles }(i,j)\mid x)=\frac{\exp f_i(x^{(ij)})}{\sum_{h}\exp f_i(x^{(ih)})},\qquad \text{waiting time to the next opportunity}\sim\mathrm{Exp}\Bigl(\sum_i\lambda_i\Bigr)
formulas.where: Actors take ministeps at a common rate and change one tie variable by a multinomial logit of the objective function after the change; the sum in the denominator includes the choice of no change. Continuous time runs over a period of length 1 between observations. Simulation starts at the first observed network and the statistics of the final network are averaged over replications, so the mean is random.

formulas.name: Simulated mean
formulas.where: Mean of the effect statistics over \(R\) simulated end networks; it converges to the model expectation after one period from the start network.

variants.saom_sim_mean: Mean statistics of simulated end networks with fixed rate and effect parameters (density, reciprocity); no estimation.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Three or more actors are needed by the tool; the definition itself has choices for any \(n\ge2\).

rsiena.behaviour: RSiena needs at least three actors (no value on empty, pair and single_node fixtures).

edge_cases.definition_gives: A complete start network is a valid state of the model; the definition simulates from it like from any other network, so the mean tie count moves from the start value towards the model's stationary value over the period.

rsiena.behaviour: From a complete starting network RSiena returns a mean tie count of about 5.0 (the stationary value, 5.4), where the reference and the exact definition oracle relax from 20 ties to 9.3 within the period; one tie removed gives 8.9 under RSiena, in line with the reference. Cause not identified.
